text:
carmen (People Ops): FYI we have Jordan moving from FT to 0.6 FTE effective 7/1 for caregiving leave (expected 10 weeks). Quick Q from manager: how do midyear elections work for 401(k) and HSA/FSA? Do we need to re-enroll or are amounts auto-prorated? cc @jay.payroll @tara-benefits

jay.payroll: We don't force re-enrollment. Deferral % stays the same unless employee changes it. Deltas: $ contributions per pay will drop because gross pay drops. Employer match follows plan rules (we match % of pay up to 4%). So match $ will be lower unless Jordan increases deferral %.

tara-benefits: For HSA: contributions are per-pay if using payroll deduction. Annual IRS limit still applies; if they contribute less earlier in year, they can increase % later to hit the annual max, but the payroll system won't auto-true-up. If Jordan wants to maintain same annual $ we recommend a temporary deferral increase. For FSA (if enrolled) the full annual election is available at the start of plan year for eligible expenses regardless of proration, but per-pay deductions are prorated.

maria-manager: Does partial pay affect eligibility for employer match or vesting schedules? Jordan is already vested per prior service. Just want to be sure match still applies.

jay.payroll: Vesting unaffected by a short-term FTE change. Match eligibility: if they're still an eligible employee per plan (active, not terminated), they get match per pay period. If pay in a period is below thresholds and deferrals are zeroed, match will be zero for that pay.

jordan-employee: Quick additional: I have an outstanding 401(k) loan and contribute pre-tax plus Roth. Will loan repayments keep coming during reduced pay? Could that push my net to negative and block deferrals?

jay.payroll: Loan repayments are treated as mandatory deductions. They continue unless you request a suspension and Fidelity approves. If gross pay in a pay results in insufficient funds after required withholdings, payroll may suppress voluntary deferrals for that period. We'll run a projection.

tara-benefits: Also note: catch-up contributions (50+) must be set explicitly. They will be applied per pay if you keep the %, so reduced pay reduces $/pay for catch-up too. If Jordan is aiming for an annual total, please request a temporary increase.

carmen (People Ops): Action items: 1) Jordan to confirm expected gross pay for first 3 pay cycles post-7/1. 2) Jay to run a payroll simulation and flag any paychecks where deferrals/loan repayments would be suppressed. 3) Tara to confirm FSA/HSA implications and how to request a temporary deferral increase in the benefits portal.

jay.payroll: I'll need projected gross and usual pre-tax elections. I can simulate by EOD tomorrow. If you DM the numbers I'll run test runs.

hr-bot: Reminder: benefits portal (https://benefits.redwood.example/) has a "Temporary payroll change" flow for midyear adjustments. For loan changes contact Fidelity rep: fidelity-client@redwood.example.

jordan-employee: Thanks — I'll DM my projected numbers and preferred contribution goal (want to keep HSA annual target same).

maria-manager: If we decide to boost % temporarily, do we need manager approval?

tara-benefits: No manager approval required — employee can change their deferral % in the portal. People Ops and Payroll should be cc'd if it's temporary so we can monitor impact on take-home pay.

carmen (People Ops): Great. We'll coordinate. Thanks everyone. :sparkles:
